title: [6/1/2024] The results of a survey in which undergraduates and postgraduates were asked about the range of books and non-printed materials
prompt: The pie charts show the results of a survey in which undergraduates and postgraduates were asked about the range of books and non-printed materials in their school library. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the satisfaction levels of undergraduate and postgraduate students regarding both books and non-print materials at an educational institution.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, undergraduate students appeared to be more satisfied with books than their postgraduate counterparts, while the opposite was true for non-print materials. Additionally, postgraduate students showed particularly high levels of dissatisfaction with non-print resources.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the books category, 37% of undergraduate students rated them as "very good", which was significantly higher than the 22% figure for postgraduate students. The figures for "satisfaction" rated by undergraduates and postgraduates stood at 35% and 28%, respectively. In addition, the proportion of undergraduates who were not satisfied with the books stood at 28%, considerably lower than the 50% of postgraduates who expressed dissatisfaction.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding non-print materials, there was a stark contrast between the two groups. While 68% of undergraduate students considered these resources to be very good, only 12% of postgraduates shared this view. Furthermore, a substantial 62% of postgraduate students rated these materials as not good, which was more than five times higher than the corresponding figure of 12% for undergraduates. The percentages of undergraduates and graduates who were satisfied were nearly similar, at 20% and 22%, respectively.
